judge_prompt_expl_example:
You read a short text and report which algorithm, if any, the text says is being used or will be used to solve a programming task.

Programming task: length of the shortest path in a directed graph with integer edge weights 0-100.

Catalogue of algorithms for this task (use these ids):
- dijkstra: Dijkstra's algorithm (also called: dijkstra, priority queue of distances). Mechanism: Dijkstra's algorithm: a single priority queue (heap) of tentative distances from s, popping the smallest distance each time (lazy deletion or decrease-key variants), one search direction.
- bf_spfa: Bellman-Ford or SPFA (also called: bellman-ford, bellman ford, bellmanford, spfa, shortest path faster, relaxation rounds). Mechanism: Bellman-Ford (repeated relaxation passes over all edges, up to n-1 rounds, possibly with early exit) or SPFA (a FIFO queue of nodes whose distance improved, often with an in-queue flag).
- bidijkstra: bidirectional Dijkstra (also called: bidirectional dijkstra, bi-directional dijkstra, two-way dijkstra). Mechanism: bidirectional Dijkstra: two Dijkstra searches, forward from s on the graph and backward from t on the reversed graph, with a meeting/stopping rule.
- floyd: Floyd-Warshall (also called: floyd-warshall, floyd warshall, floyd, warshall, all-pairs). Mechanism: Floyd-Warshall: all-pairs shortest paths with a triple loop over k, i, j updating dist[i][j] = min(dist[i][j], dist[i][k] + dist[k][j]).
- dial: Dial's bucket-queue algorithm (also called: dial's, dial , bucket queue, bucket-queue, buckets indexed by distance). Mechanism: Dial's algorithm: Dijkstra with a bucket queue, i.e. an array or dict of buckets indexed by distance, scanned in increasing distance order instead of a binary heap.

Definitions:
- planned: the id of the catalogue algorithm that the text says is being, or will be, used or implemented. An algorithm that the text names only as forbidden, avoided, banned or not allowed is NOT planned (it goes to negated). If the text says that a specific method which is NOT in the catalogue is being or will be used (for example a genetic algorithm, a neural network, random guessing or any other named technique), answer "other" -- never "none_named" in that case. Answer "none_named" only when the text names no method at all as being or going to be used.
- mentioned: every catalogue id the text names in any way (by name, alias or unmistakable description).
- negated: the catalogue ids the text names only as forbidden, avoided or excluded.

Text:
"""
<TEXT>
"""

Answer with one JSON object only, no other words: {"planned": "<id or none_named or other>", "mentioned": ["<id>", ...], "negated": ["<id>", ...]}
